title: Slow-cooker chicken fajitas
subtitle: Tender spiced chicken with peppers and onion for wrapping
excerpt: Chicken breasts cooked with three colours of pepper, onion, and Tex-Mex spices. Shred and pile into warm tortilla wraps with soured cream and guacamole.
sourceNotes: Fajitas are a Tex-Mex dish originating in southern Texas, originally made with skirt steak. Chicken fajitas became popular in British homes from the 1990s and are now a staple of slow-cooker cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the shredded chicken and pepper mix in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat in a pan.
recipe.batchNotes: Excellent batch recipe. The filling keeps for 4 days in the fridge and heats well in a pan or microwave.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling ahead and refrigerate. Warm tortillas and all toppings fresh at serving time.

content.text: The slow cooker does almost all the work here. The chicken and peppers cook together in their own juices, and by the end the chicken is tender enough to shred into the filling with two forks. The only thing you lose compared to a griddle pan is the charred edges; you gain everything else.

Three colours of pepper give the filling colour and a good variety of flavour. Red peppers are sweetest and soften the most. Green peppers keep more of their texture and add a slightly bitter note that balances the spices.
Serve in warm tortilla wraps with soured cream, guacamole, grated cheese, and sliced spring onion.
Add all the dry spices and salt to a small bowl and mix. Rub the spice mix all over {{chicken-breast}} chicken breasts.
Place the sliced onion in the base of the slow cooker. Lay the spice-rubbed chicken on top. Scatter over the sliced {{pepper-red}}, {{pepper-green}}, and {{pepper-yellow}} peppers.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 3 to 4 hours. The chicken should be very tender. Shred it with two forks directly in the pot and mix it through the peppers and onion. Squeeze over {{lime}} lime juice. Serve in warm tortilla wraps.

rows.cause: The peppers and chicken both release liquid during cooking.
rows.fix: Remove the filling with a slotted spoon, leaving excess liquid in the pot. Set the slow cooker to HIGH with the lid off for 15 minutes to reduce the liquid, then stir the filling back in.

rows.cause: Chicken breast cooks through quickly and dries out if cooked past 4 hours on LOW.
rows.fix: Next time check at 3 hours. The chicken is done when it shreds easily. Stir the shredded meat through the liquid and pepper mix, which will re-moisten it.

rows.cause: Peppers soften significantly during a 4-hour cook.
rows.fix: This is normal for slow-cooker fajitas. For more texture, add the peppers in the last hour only. Alternatively, quickly stir-fry a handful of fresh sliced pepper to add at serving time.

rows.symptom: The spice level is too mild
rows.cause: Ground spices added at the start lose intensity over a long, low cook.
rows.fix: Add an extra pinch of chilli powder at the end and a fresh squeeze of lime to lift the whole dish.

content.text: Fajitas crossed from Tex-Mex restaurants into British home kitchens in the 1990s and have stayed ever since. The slow-cooker version has become a fixture of weeknight meal planning. It suits families because it is adaptable: mild for children, spiced up for adults, and served at the table where everyone builds their own.
